title: check.py checks every line of a ledger path:line range citation, not only its first
goal: check.py's ledger citation rule (ST-ctomsu4i, 815428cd1) refuses a range citation such as x.md:7-9 in a root's _answers.md or _gaps.md when any line of the range names no line of a tagged fact, not only when its first line does; found by the SP-caqrexqw review.

run: import sys,os,tempfile,types; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import check; d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); os.mkdir(d+'/a'); n=chr(10); open(d+'/a/x.md','w').write(n.join(['# T','','- Fact one. [DOC S1]','','## Reference','','| a | b |',''])); open(d+'/_answers.md','w').write(n.join(['# A','','- see a/x.md:3-7',''])); e=check.ledger_citation_errors(types.SimpleNamespace(path=d,name='fx')); print(e); sys.exit(0 if e else 1)

notes: Premise: run at planning (SP-5i4itd2d): LEDGER_CITE on 'a/x.md:7-9' yields line 7 only, the range end is never read, and the first check (a ledger citing a/x.md:3-7 whose line 7 is a table row) finds no error: reproduces. The -k ledger_citation check passes before the work and stays in as a guard that the first-line rule holds (the existing test). Order: after ST-z5uh6oj7 (test_live_kb.py) and before ST-2bly3tq5 (check.py).
